newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to Slovnaft drag Slovak SAX index down.
newsitem.headline: Losses to Slovnaft drag Slovak SAX index down.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with losses to the average price of Slovnaft pulling the SAX down 1.48 points to 204.65.
Brokers said they expected a flat period in the near future, with steel maker VSZ the only stock capable of nudging the market higher.
"Foreign investors, who boosted trading during the last week, have probably already fulfilled their orders and have temporarily left the market," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
VSZ closed up five crowns at 670, with 569 shares traded.
"VSZ is on the rise at the moment and I think it will attract the attention of the investors, if there is any (attention) to appear in the next days," Sykora said.

Oil refinery Slovnaft closed unchanged at 910 crowns, but traded 19 shares at an average price which was 2.67 percent lower. Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down 20 crowns at 1,900 crowns, with only 14 shares traded.
Overall volume, boosted by direct trading, increased to 549,859 shares, from 484,258 on Tuesday, while turnover eased to 325.55 million crowns, from 565.33 million.
Only 874 shares were traded on the BSE floor on Wednesday, with turnover of 718,227 crowns.
